root_cause: The navigation controller incorrectly sets aria-activedescendant to the highlighted item's text content instead of its id when navigating via arrow keys.
repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener on the input field that corrects aria-activedescendant to the id of the currently highlighted suggestion (identified by aria-selected='true') whenever ArrowDown or ArrowUp is pressed, ensuring the attribute references the element's id.
expected_accessibility_effect: Arrowing through suggestions will now update the input's aria-activedescendant to match the id of the active option, allowing assistive technologies to announce the highlighted option correctly.
functional_risks: Potential duplicate setting of aria-activedescendant if navigation controller also updates it; this is harmless as the value will be the same.
If the list structure changes and no element with aria-selected='true' is found, the attribute will be removed, which is safe and does not break core functionality.
verification_requirements: After typing 'ma' and pressing ArrowDown once, the input's aria-activedescendant should equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_0'.
After a second ArrowDown, aria-activedescendant should equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_1'.
Pressing Enter should submit the highlighted suggestion's value ('Marina Park') into the form.
Mouse clicks on suggestions should continue to work as before.
Ensure no regression in existing keyboard navigation (e.g., ArrowUp, Escape) or screen reader announcements.
